title: A predictive microscopic theory of cuprate superconductivity

concept.text: Discovered Materials grand challenge 01: explain how superconductivity arises from the cuprates' unusual normal state, and predict their phase diagram from a microscopic theory. Sources given: https://discoveredmaterials.com/grand-challenges/.

page.title: A predictive microscopic theory of cuprate superconductivity
page.definition: A theory starting from electron and atomic interactions explains superconductivity—zero resistance and magnetic-flux expulsion—in cuprates, layered copper oxides. It predicts their phase diagram, the phases present versus temperature and carrier concentration, and explains the conducting state above the transition.

goal.need: A report published on 6 May 1993 established superconductivity near 133 K in mixed-phase Hg–Ba–Ca–Cu–O material using magnetic and resistance measurements. Predicting such transition temperatures from atomic interactions would support materials selection; the US Department of Energy’s 2006 workshop identified quantitative theory of individual superconductors as a research priority.

completion.title: Discovered Materials judges a microscopic theory to satisfy every criterion of its cuprate challenge.
completion.criterion: Discovered Materials accepts a reproducible microscopic theory under Challenge 01. Its 12 benchmarks cover the phase diagram; gap symmetry and magnitude; pseudogap spectra; resistivity; specific heat and entropy; superfluid density; antiferromagnetism; magnetic excitations; charge order; elastic and symmetry-breaking responses; and local pairing. These must follow quantitatively from a physically justified Hamiltonian, the equation specifying the system’s energy, without fitting each observable independently. Calibration observations must be distinguished from independent predictions.
completion.set_by: Discovered Materials, Grand Challenges Official Rules, sections 4–5, incorporating the Challenge 01 description.
completion.threshold_quote: A challenge is "solved" only when a submission meets every success criterion in its Challenge Description
completion.basis: This is an external adjudication test for the stated breakthrough. The sponsor requires every success criterion and retains the decision on qualification. Its technical description requires a common microscopic framework and reproducible predictions, but publishes no numerical acceptance tolerances. This is a prize criterion, not a field-wide consensus standard; Challenge 01 remains listed as open.

milestones.title: A cuprate exhibits half-quantum flux in a phase-sensitive test of d-wave pairing.
milestones.criterion: Observe spontaneous half-integer flux quantization in a deliberately frustrated cuprate Josephson geometry, with unfrustrated controls. Tsuei et al. reported h/(4e) flux in a three-junction YBa₂Cu₃O₇−δ ring at 4.2 K, absent in two-junction controls, on 25 July 1994. Here h is Planck’s constant and e the elementary charge. This establishes a pairing-symmetry constraint, not its microscopic cause.
milestones.set_by: The phase-sensitive pairing-symmetry convention reviewed by Tsuei and Kirtley; the cited initial demonstration used YBa₂Cu₃O₇−δ.
milestones.threshold_quote: the half-integer flux-quantum effect as an unambiguous signature

milestones.title: A theory predicts local pair-density changes from charge-transfer energy.
milestones.criterion: Predict local pair-density response to charge-transfer energy, the energy for transferring charge between oxygen and copper. On 6 September 2022, O’Mahony et al. reported d nP/dE ≈ −0.81 ± 0.17 eV⁻¹ for mean-normalized pair density in Bi₂Sr₂CaCu₂O₈₊ₓ at p ≈ 0.17 holes per Cu, compared with a prediction near −0.9 eV⁻¹. Energy and pair-density analyses covered 7 and 13 structural-modulation periods, respectively. This tests a local relation, not a transition temperature.
milestones.set_by: Discovered Materials, benchmark table, row 12; the threshold is tabulated.

milestones.title: A theory predicts the cuprate pseudogap’s spectra and evolution.
milestones.criterion: Predict electron spectra, pseudogap energy and their temperature–doping dependence. A pseudogap is depleted low-energy electronic spectral weight above the superconducting transition. Šimkovic et al., published on 20 September 2024, obtained a Hubbard-model pseudogap using controlled diagrammatic Monte Carlo calculations in the infinite-size limit. Their calculations covered repulsion U/t ≤ 8, hole concentrations up to 0.20 per site and kB T/t from 0.07 to 0.25. Here t is hopping energy and kB Boltzmann’s constant. Model spectral proxies do not establish quantitative agreement with a particular cuprate.
milestones.set_by: Discovered Materials, benchmark table, row 4; the threshold is tabulated.

milestones.title: A theory predicts cuprate resistivity versus temperature and doping.
milestones.criterion: Predict resistivity’s magnitude and temperature–doping dependence. Huang et al. reported approximately temperature-linear resistivity in an 8 × 8 Hubbard lattice with U/t = 6, next-neighbor hopping t′/t = −0.25 and kB T/t down to 0.2, on 22 November 2019. Legros et al. measured temperature-linear resistivity in one Bi₂Sr₂CaCu₂O₈₊δ film at nominal hole concentration 0.23, using fields up to 58 T. These provide a model result and an experimental target, rather than a material-specific microscopic prediction.
milestones.set_by: Discovered Materials, benchmark table, row 5; the threshold is tabulated.

milestones.title: A theory predicts superconducting domes across cuprate material families.
milestones.criterion: Predict T_c(p), including both dome edges, its optimum and maximum, and family differences; p is hole concentration per Cu. On 19 December 2024, Qu et al. reported a dome-shaped pairing regime in a t–t′–J model on cylinders up to 6 sites wide, down to kB T/J ≈ 0.06. Its highest pairing-crossover scale was about 0.15J/kB for t′/t > 0, corresponding to electron doping in their convention. J is magnetic exchange energy. A cylinder pairing crossover does not establish bulk, material-specific superconducting transition temperatures.
milestones.set_by: Discovered Materials, benchmark table, row 1; the threshold is tabulated.

not_found: No numerical acceptance tolerances, prescribed doping grid or minimum family count were found in the challenge description or official rules.
The publisher’s full-text page for “Origin and fate of the pseudogap in the doped Hubbard model” returned HTTP 403; its author manuscript was accessible.

results.finding: Hubbard-model calculation, infinite-size limit: pseudogap regime mapped across five temperatures.
results.detail: The calculation tracks spectral proxies and pseudogap crossovers over temperature and doping, but does not report the pseudogap energy or quantitative agreement with a particular cuprate. It uses imaginary-frequency data without analytic continuation.

results.finding: Three-band Emery model calculation, no physical sample: pseudogap occurs at hole doping 0.05–0.15.
results.detail: The calculation reports spectral evolution with doping and temperature and qualitative agreement with cuprate observations. It does not report the pseudogap energy or its temperature–doping dependence.
results.quote:
For the lowest temperatures that we analyzed, we
find the pseudogap regime in a doping range of δn ∈
[0.05, 0.15].

results.finding: In an 8 × 8 Hubbard lattice, the low-temperature resistivity coefficient fell roughly threefold as hole doping increased from 0.1 to 0.3.
results.detail: The calculation found approximately temperature-linear resistivity down to T/t = 0.2 for U/t = 6 and t′/t = −0.25. It is a model result, not a material-specific prediction of cuprate resistivity.
results.quote:

results.finding: One Bi2212 film showed temperature-linear resistivity at nominal hole doping p = 0.23.
results.detail: Fields up to 58 T suppressed superconductivity. The measured resistivity provides an experimental target; the Planckian estimate uses measured material properties and is not a microscopic prediction of resistivity across temperature and doping.
results.quote:
The raw data at H = 55 T reveal a perfectly linear 
T dependence of ρ(T) down to the lowest accessible temperature 
(Fig. 1a).

results.finding: Hubbard-model resistivity compared with experiments on 3 cuprate compounds gives best agreement at U ≈ 8–10 eV.
results.detail: The model covers temperature and doping dependence, but its coupling is chosen to match experiment and a doping-dependent residual resistivity is added. Agreement for LCCO is good only below about 150 K; higher-temperature curvature is not reproduced.

results.detail: The dome is a pairing regime for the electron-doped model convention. The source does not establish bulk, material-specific T_c(p), both dome edges, or differences across cuprate families.

results.finding: Four cuprate families studied; the superconducting order parameter has a dome peaking at hole doping δ ≈ 0.05–0.1.
results.detail: The calculations concern ground-state order, not a full prediction of T_c(p). The proposed optimal-T_c scaling uses experimental comparisons; neither T_c dome edge nor its optimum is predicted across the families.

results.finding: Calculations for 10 compounds across two cuprate families found a minimum effective plane doping of approximately 4% for superconductivity.
results.detail: The study estimates zero-temperature superconducting order parameters and family differences. Its zero-temperature solver does not predict T_c(p), its maximum, or both dome edges.
results.quote:
This explains why the superconducting order
parameter vanishes in the inner planes for n ≥ 4: The
effective normal-state hole doping remains below a critical
threshold of approximately 4%, in remarkable agreement
with experiments [67].

results.finding: For one cuprate, CCO, the theory estimates an ambient-pressure maximum Tc of approximately 180 K.
results.detail: The calculation also captures qualitative pairing trends across three cuprate compounds. It uses a weak-coupling conversion from pairing gap to Tc, ignores temperature effects, and does not predict both edges of material-specific Tc(p) domes.
results.quote:
